## Proposed change
This PR continues the work started in #38725 by @MrHarcombe and #45149 by @hencoappel.
This change exposes the 3-hourly and daily forecast updates from the MetOffice service. By default only the currently exposed 3-hourly sensor entities will be enabled (to save having too many entities enabled by default) but both 3-hourly and daily weather entities, with forecast data, will be enabled by default.
Fixes https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/35196

## The problem
The met office weather componant does not provide a 5 day forecast in Home Assistant in the same way other weather integrations do (i.e. darkSky) even though the API is capable of returning 5 day forecast data.


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.108.9
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known):
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): HassOS VM, Supervisor 220
- Integration causing this issue: Met Office
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/metoffice/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
weather:
  - platform: metoffice
    api_key: !secret api_metoffice
    latitude: !secret metoffice_lat
    longitude: !secret metoffice_lon
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information
It may be worth noting that the Met Office have launched a new API called DataHub which will eventually replace the current DataPoint API
https://metoffice.apiconnect.ibmcloud.com/metoffice/production/

I'm also seeing this issue and would prefer to use the UK Met Office for forecasts rather than Norwegian Meteorological Institute.

The UK Met Office forecasts are pretty accurate for where I live but unfortunately the Norwegian Meteorological Institute forecasts are wildly different from our real weather. Not having a reliable weather service for the UK is something of an issue which makes potentially valuable weather-based automations completely unusable. Unfortunately without this simple service Home Assistant can never be my main platform for home automation.  I'm guessing that many people here in the UK are in the same boat. I'd invest the time and fix this myself if I knew how...

Agree with previous comments.
I will investigate further, but it does look like a restricted UK weather forecast is a possible deal-breaker for allowing me to integrate my heating system control within HA. Pity, but maybe I'm missing something and it is/will become possible
Is there any progress with this? I see that #45149 was opened to finish up the great work done on #38725, but it's been marked stale 2 days ago.

I have just moved over to Met Office from Dark Sky seen as their API is being turned off soon and this forecast would be great.

I see that [#45149](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/45149) has had some activity 14 days ago so looks like there has been some work done since @sym0nd0 looked last.

Fingers crossed this is close to being implemented.. Met office weather is the most accurate. I dont really need the forecast for automations but it is nice to be able to see the information at glance like with the default weather integration and OpenWeatherMap. But I do use the current weather status to open and close some south facing blinds in the evening to avoid glare on the TV... an over engineered solution to being lazy :)

I too would like to see the 5 day forecast represented in the entity list. Can I also add to that the current atmospheric pressure? This would be useful in automations for creating a digital barometer and tracking the speed at which it changes to indicate stormy weather approaching.
